description: The last three shots of MarmotCroonsFull, generated on their own. The full sixteen-shot run holds every finished shot in memory as a previous_result - about 460 MB a shot on top of a 51 GB resident pipeline - and was OOM-killed on shot fourteen with 3.3 GB left. The thirteen shots it had already written are reused as they are; this generates the remainder with identical settings, prompts and audio slices, and the stitch joins all sixteen.

variables.shot_14_over_shoulder:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the cartoon marmot in <Picture 1>: standing upright on its hind legs at a chrome microphone on a boom stand, its fur banded brown and cream with dark mask-like patches around the eyes, a pale muzzle, long white whiskers and alert rounded ears.
<Picture 1> is a subject and setting reference only. It establishes who <Subject 1> is - fur, face, build and the microphone it sings into - and the club around it, its stage dressing, haze, warm amber light and the guitar in soft focus. It carries no compositional detail: no framing, no shot size, no camera position, no camera height and no lens. The composition of this clip is the one described below and is not taken from <Picture 1>.
<Audio 1> is the piece of the song covering this part of the video, a slow jazz number <Subject 1> sings into the microphone.

summary:
[image reference + audio song reference] The target video is an over-the-shoulder shot from behind <Subject 1>, looking past it out into the room, in one continuous shot.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the fur banding, eye patches, muzzle, whiskers, ears and proportions of <Picture 1> are kept exactly, with the head, jaw and shoulders newly animated to sing.
<Picture 1>: partially_copy - identity, wardrobe, set, palette and lighting are taken from it; framing, shot size, camera position, camera height and lens are NOT. This clip is an over-the-shoulder shot from behind, the face away from camera, which is deliberately different from the framing of <Picture 1>.
<Audio 1>: partially_copy - the piece of the song covering this part of the video is reused as the soundtrack. This stretch of the recording is largely instrumental and <Subject 1>'s mouth is not in frame, so no lip movement is depicted; the shot carries the music on its light, haze and the subject's posture instead.

detailed_description:
The target video is in the warmly lit, softly rendered cartoon style of <Picture 1>. [Shot 1] An over-the-shoulder shot sits behind and just above <Subject 1>, looking past the back of its head and one ear out across the microphone into the dark room beyond, the stage lights flaring toward the lens through the haze. Its face is turned away from the camera and is not seen. The banded fur across its back and shoulders is sharp in the near frame. <Subject 1>'s mouth is not visible in this framing and no attempt is made to show it. Its body keeps the easy time of the music - a small sway, a settling of the shoulders - and nothing in the shot depends on the lip movement. The lighting, colour and contrast match <Picture 1> exactly and are steady from the first frame to the last, with smooth fur and no grain, speckle or hardened edges. The camera holds this framing statically throughout, with no reframing, no zoom and no cut.

overall_soundscape:
The song of <Audio 1> carries the shot, the vocal close and warm at the microphone. Under it, the instrumental carrying the room, a low crowd murmur ahead in the dark and the faint hum of the amplifiers.

non_diegetic_music:
None - the music is the diegetic performance of <Audio 1>.
